title: Hand each answer to the message it answers

blocks.text: An acquirer's link carries the messages of many terminals at once, and the host sends a few of its own. `Inbox` keeps every message the acquirer has sent and not yet seen answered. When something arrives, `deliver` hands it to the sent message it answers, or returns `null` so the caller can log it.

`deliver` already works. Finish `answers(sent, incoming)` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Inbox.java`. When you're done, every answer reaches the message it belongs to, including answers to advices and to their repeats, and nothing else reaches anyone. About ten lines.
The tests send messages from several terminals with STANs that sometimes coincide.

cases.says: an authorization, a purchase and an echo each receive their own answer, and the sent messages stay unchanged
an answer with another STAN, or the host's own request, reaches no waiting message
a response of another class, such as an 0210 with the STAN of a waiting 0100, answers some other message
an advice is answered by an advice response, so an 0220 takes an 0230 and not an 0210
a repeat is answered like the message it repeats, so an 0421 takes an 0430
two terminals with the same STAN each receive their own answer, because the terminal ID is part of the match

origin.section: 4.1. The Third Digit Pairs Every Message With Its Answer

concepts: The MTI pairs kinds of message, so a response belongs to a request only when it also carries the request's STAN and terminal ID.

A message's answer keeps its class and raises the function digit by one, so a request is answered by a response and an advice by an advice response, and a repeat is answered like the message it repeats.
